notes:
CONTRADICTION — the "sort button" does not exist in code. The shortDescription (3rd super() arg, OverpackedExtensionsModule.java:39-40) promises "and a Quark-style sort button"; docs/modules/overpacked_extensions.md:94-96 claims "The sort screen hook is registered manually on the client only when Overpacked is present"; README.md:231 speaks of "backpack keybinds + sort button". None of it is true: `grep -rn -i sort` over the whole module directory returns exactly four hits, all javadoc/comment (config javadoc:19, module javadoc:24, the shortDescription string:40, a stale comment:49). There is no screen hook, no sort packet, no button class. The correct position is in the module's own javadoc (lines 24-26), in README.md:186 and in docs section "Sorting & searching — use Quark, don't reimplement": sorting/searching are deliberately NOT reimplemented; you get Quark's own buttons by whitelisting Overpacked's screen class in Quark's config. Two more leftovers from the deleted feature: OverpackedExtensionsModule.java:49 says "Backpack open/sort packets" although only one packet type exists, and the class javadoc line 14 announces "three quality-of-life features" while its own <ol> lists two.

MODULE STRUCTURE — two features, one enabled flag. The module bundles a slowdown override (SlowdownFeature) and the backpack keybinds; both share the module-level `enabled`, each has its own sub-toggle. Note the asymmetry: `backpack_keys_enabled` is a real boolean toggle, but the slowdown feature has no on/off switch — it is "off" only in the sense that slowdown_multiplier = 1.0 reproduces vanilla Overpacked behaviour.

DEFAULT IS A GAMEPLAY CHANGE. slowdown_multiplier defaults to **0.0**, i.e. out of the box this module removes Overpacked's full-backpack movement penalty entirely. A doc writer should say that plainly; readers will assume a neutral 1.0 default.

SLOWDOWN IS SERVER-SIDE, RUNS WITHOUT OVERPACKED AND IS NOT TAG-SCOPED. SlowdownFeature references no Overpacked classes — it re-implements Overpacked's formula by reading the vanilla CUSTOM_DATA "Count" int on every main-inventory stack plus the offhand (SlowdownFeature.java:53-66) and bails out on the client (SlowdownFeature.java:45-47). It is registered unconditionally (OverpackedExtensionsModule.java:47), so it ticks for every player on every server even on packs without Overpacked. Consequence: any item from any mod carrying a CUSTOM_DATA "Count" >= 27 would be counted as a loaded backpack. It also removes and re-adds the `overpacked:speed` transient attribute modifier every single server tick for every player, even when the computed slowdown is 0 (SlowdownFeature.java:72-79) — the modifier is always present, just with amount 0. That unconditional remove+re-add is exactly how the override wins: Overpacked's own NORMAL-priority modifier is replaced each tick by ours at LOW priority.

KEYBIND CLASH WITH OVERPACKED 2.x — verified, not just documented. Disassembling libs/overpacked-2.0.1-1.21.1-neoforge.jar (net/nycto_team/overpacked/registry/ModKeyBinds) shows `key.overpacked.take_off_backpack`, KeyConflictContext.IN_GAME, KEYSYM, `bipush 66` = GLFW_KEY_B — the same default as this module's "open main compartment". On a fresh profile both fire. Ours uses the 4-arg KeyMapping constructor, i.e. the default UNIVERSAL conflict context, so the clash is real in-game. Documented at docs/modules/overpacked_extensions.md:29-31; ours sits in the Controls category "Vanilla+ Additions" (the doc's wording "Vanilla Plus Additions" does not match en_us.json:138).

CLIENT SIDE DOES NOT CHECK THE MODULE STATE. BackpackKeybinds/BackpackKeysClientEvents are plain @EventBusSubscriber(Dist.CLIENT) classes with no module-enabled gate: the three keybinds always appear in the Controls menu and a keypress always sends a packet, even when the module or backpack_keys_enabled is off. The server-side handler is what silently drops it (OverpackedExtensionsModule.java:70-72). It also sends regardless of whether the player wears a backpack — the server answers with the "You aren't wearing a giant backpack." actionbar message (OverpackedGuiBridge.java:84-88). All three user-visible messages are actionbar (displayClientMessage(..., true)).

THE TRANSIENT HELPER ENTITY is the core trick and its side effects are player-visible. Overpacked's GUI is entity-bound, so opening the worn backpack spawns a real (noPhysics, no-gravity) GiantBackpack entity 1.5 blocks in front of the player along their horizontal look vector — falling back to inside the player when that spot collides (OverpackedGuiBridge.java:112-135) — opens the menu on it one tick later via a TickTask (:166-173), then writes getPickResult()'s CUSTOM_DATA back onto the worn Curios stack on close/logout and discards it. Other players can briefly see that backpack. If the original Curios slot no longer holds a giant backpack, the write-back falls back to the player's inventory and finally to dropping the stack, so items are never lost (:253-257). A hard crash while the GUI is open leaves the edited items on the entity in-world rather than in the worn item (docs lines 109-112).

TWO NON-OBVIOUS INVARIANTS worth preserving in any rewrite: (1) the ModList gate MUST stay in OverpackedCompat, a class with zero Overpacked types — putting it on OverpackedGuiBridge crashed mod construction with NoClassDefFoundError: net/nycto_team/overpacked/menu/GiantBackpackMenu on packs without Overpacked (beta.70 regression, OverpackedCompat.java:8-14). (2) On write-back, a null CUSTOM_DATA must CLEAR the worn item's CUSTOM_DATA, not be skipped — Overpacked returns a bare stack for an emptied backpack, and keeping the stale tag duplicated the old contents on the next open (OverpackedGuiBridge.java:241-252, the else-branch at :250-252).

SIDE-POCKET LOCK (Overpacked 2.x only). Right/left compartments are overpacked:backpack_pocket upgrades; the unlock is encoded as the mere PRESENCE of RightCell/LeftCell in CUSTOM_DATA — the stored value is always 0 and meaningless, so it must be checked with contains(), never by reading the value (OverpackedGuiBridge.java:54-76). Pressing a locked compartment's key reports "That backpack compartment isn't unlocked yet." instead of opening, because the helper entity builds all three containers regardless and opening would grant the upgrade for free. Overpacked 1.x has no such concept.

BOBO LIB. Not an integration of ours and never referenced in module code, but Overpacked 2.x hard-requires it (its GiantBackpack calls BU.ShrinkCreative), so it sits on the compile and localRuntime classpath (build.gradle:176/179) and is listed under Requirements in the module doc. Mention it only as "ships with Overpacked 2.x".

NO DECLARED DEPENDENCIES, BUT THE JARS ARE IN THE REPO. Neither src/main/resources/META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml (its only [[dependencies]] entries are neoforge, create, toughasnails, sable, bluemap, minecraft) nor the standaloneModules entry (build.gradle:451 — no moduleDeps, no mixins, no dataGlobs) declares overpacked or curios; everything is runtime ModList gating. Overpacked/Curios/Bobo Lib are compileOnly + localRuntime jars (build.gradle:175-180) and — unlike sable/ToughAsNails/Quark/Zeta, which .gitignore:72-75 excludes — they are COMMITTED to the repository (git ls-files libs/ lists overpacked-2.0.1-1.21.1-neoforge.jar, curios-neoforge-9.5.1+1.21.1.jar, bobo_lib-1.1-1.21.1-neoforge.jar). This module therefore compiles from a clean clone; it is not one of the modules blocked by the missing-jar problem in CLAUDE.md.

VERSION HISTORY CAVEAT. v1.0.0-beta.56 is when this *directory* first appeared, and the tag sits on the very commit 09907a8 ("refactor(overpacked_extensions): merge slowdown + backpack_keys into one module", 2026-07-28; `git tag --points-at 09907a8` = v1.0.0-beta.56). The features are older: overpacked_slowdown shipped in v0.7.0 (commit 1e3d803, 2026-04-30) and overpacked_backpack_keys in v1.0.0-beta.31 (commit 21e12d7, 2026-07-06). Users upgrading across beta.56 lost the old module ids and their config sections.

L10N. All six lang files (cs_cz, de_at, de_de, en_us, es_es, fr_fr) carry all six keys; en_us.json:145-147 (keybinds) and 175-177 (messages: compartment_locked, no_backpack, unavailable). No item/block/entity/command/recipe/mixin of its own — no DeferredRegister, no RegisterCommandsEvent, no mixin package under mixin/ and no mention in vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json. The module registers exactly one network payload (vanillaplusadditions:open_backpack_compartment, registrar version "1", play-to-server, VAR_INT compartment; 0 = center/main 55 slots, 1 = right 28, 2 = left 28).

LEFTOVER HELPERS (fixed 2026-09-20, v1.0.0-beta.87): SESSIONS is a static map, so a server restart with the GUI open leaves the helper entity saved in the world with no session behind it — onContainerClose then treats it as somebody's real placed backpack and leaves it alone. Two consequences, both observed in play: the helper sits inside the player (the noCollision fallback in openFor), and Overpacked's place_predicate — EntitySelector.NO_SPECTATORS.and(Entity::isPickable) — makes Utils.PlaceBackpack return InteractionResultHolder.pass() for ANY pickable entity whose inflated box contains the player's eye position, so placing a backpack from the hand silently does nothing, with no message and nothing in the log; and the helper's contents are a copy of the worn backpack's, so breaking it duplicates them. The fix tags the helper with Entity.addTag("vpa_backpack_helper") before addFreshEntity and discards any tagged helper in EntityJoinLevelEvent when loadedFromDisk() is true — the flag separates a leftover from a freshly spawned one without depending on the order of addFreshEntity and SESSIONS.put. The spawn position was deliberately NOT changed: spawning inside the player when the spot in front is blocked is intended, so the helper stays out of the crosshair.
oneLiner: Open the compartments of the giant backpack you are wearing with a keypress instead of taking it off, and dial the full-backpack movement slowdown down to anything you like — including off entirely.

optionalMods.whatItAdds: The whole point of the module. With Overpacked present, the keybinds open the worn giant backpack through Overpacked's own GiantBackpackMenu/Screen, and the slowdown override rescales the real penalty. Without it, the GUI bridge's event handlers are never registered (OverpackedExtensionsModule.java:57-59) and a keypress only prints "Overpacked backpack access is unavailable." (OverpackedExtensionsModule.java:80-84); the slowdown handler still ticks but finds nothing to rescale. Both Overpacked 1.x and 2.x are supported — the restore path is chosen from the major version (OverpackedCompat.java:32-35).

Required alongside Overpacked for the keybind feature: the worn backpack is located and written back through the Curios inventory (any slot type, matched by the #overpacked:giant_backpacks item tag — CuriosBackpackAccess.java:25-26, 45-55). isAvailable() is false without it, so the bridge is never registered. Overpacked hard-requires Curios anyway, so in practice they are present or absent together.

Documentation-only — there is NO Quark code, no Quark type reference and no ModList check for Quark anywhere in this module (grep -i quark over the module directory hits four javadoc/comment lines and nothing else). Quark's own sort button and search bar appear on Overpacked's backpack screen once the player adds "net.nycto_team.overpacked.screen.GiantBackpackScreen" to Quark's "Allowed Screens" list in config/quark-common.toml. Without Quark (or without that config line) there is no sort button anywhere. Note the Quark jar on the compile classpath (build.gradle:160) belongs to pathfinder_quills, not to this module. Kept in this list only because it is a real, user-facing capability of the feature — a doc must not present it as a code integration.

shortDescription: Quality-of-life extensions for Overpacked giant backpacks: configurable slowdown override, keybinds to open worn compartments, and a Quark-style sort button.
